mcqs.question: Which of the following lists correctly shows the order of metals from most reactive to least reactive according to the NCERT reactivity series?

options.A: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
options.B: Sodium, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
options.C: Potassium, Calcium, Sodium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
options.D: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Zinc, Aluminium, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold

mcqs.answer: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
mcqs.explanation: The NCERT reactivity series lists metals in decreasing reactivity as: Potassium > Sodium > Calcium > Magnesium > Aluminium > Zinc > Iron > Nickel > Tin > Lead > Hydrogen > Copper > Silver > Gold. Option A matches this exact order, while the other options have misplaced elements.

mcqs.question: When a strip of zinc metal is immersed in an aqueous solution of copper sulphate, which of the following best describes the observed reaction?

options.B: Zinc dissolves, and copper metal is deposited on the zinc strip.
options.C: Copper dissolves, and zinc metal is deposited on the copper.
options.D: Both zinc and copper precipitate as insoluble compounds.

mcqs.answer: Zinc dissolves, and copper metal is deposited on the zinc strip.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it displaces copper from its salt solution. Zinc atoms lose electrons to form Zn²⁺ ions, while Cu²⁺ ions gain electrons and deposit as copper metal on the zinc surface. Options A, C, and D describe outcomes that contradict the series.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the behavior of a metal that is higher in the reactivity series from a metal that is lower when each is placed in the other's salt solution?

options.A: The higher‑reactive metal will displace the lower‑reactive metal from its salt solution, but the lower‑reactive metal will not displace the higher‑reactive metal.
options.B: Both metals will displace each other from each other's salt solutions.
options.C: Neither metal will cause any displacement in the other's salt solution.
options.D: The lower‑reactive metal will displace the higher‑reactive metal from its salt solution.

mcqs.answer: The higher‑reactive metal will displace the lower‑reactive metal from its salt solution, but the lower‑reactive metal will not displace the higher‑reactive metal.
mcqs.explanation: A metal can displace another metal from its salt solution only if it is higher in the reactivity series. The reverse is impossible because the lower‑reactive metal lacks the tendency to lose electrons. Hence option A correctly captures this distinction; the other options contradict the series.

mcqs.question: Arrange the following metals in order of decreasing reactivity according to the reactivity series: Magnesium (Mg), Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu).
mcqs.explanation: In the series, magnesium is more reactive than iron, and iron is more reactive than copper. Therefore the correct decreasing order is Mg > Fe > Cu. Options B, C, and D place at least one metal in the wrong position.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals will NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid under normal conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Metals above hydrogen in the series (e.g., Zn, Fe, Mg) can displace hydrogen from dilute HCl, producing H₂ gas. Copper lies below hydrogen, so it does not react with dilute HCl. Hence option C is correct; the others will react.

mcqs.question: A piece of metal A is placed in an aqueous solution of metal B nitrate. Metal A dissolves and metal B is deposited on its surface. Which pair of metals could represent A and B?
mcqs.explanation: Iron is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so iron can displace copper from copper nitrate, leading to dissolution of iron and deposition of copper. Option B reflects this correct pair. In option A the roles are reversed, and options C and D involve metals that would not produce the described observation under normal conditions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: A student claims that when a piece of silver is placed in a solution of copper sulphate, silver will replace copper because silver is a metal. Which of the following best addresses this misconception?

options.A: Silver is actually more reactive than copper, so it will replace copper.
options.B: Silver is less reactive than copper; therefore no displacement occurs.
options.C: Both metals are equally reactive, so a partial displacement occurs.
options.D: Displacement depends only on the concentration of the solution, not reactivity.

mcqs.answer: Silver is less reactive than copper; therefore no displacement occurs.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series shows copper above silver. A metal can displace another only if it is higher in the series. Since silver is lower, it cannot displace copper from copper sulphate; no reaction is observed. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they ignore the series hierarchy.

mcqs.question: Given that potassium reacts vigorously with water but gold does not react with water, which of the following conclusions about their positions in the reactivity series is most appropriate?

options.A: Potassium is placed below gold in the series.
options.B: Gold is placed above potassium in the series.
options.C: Potassium is placed above gold in the series.
options.D: Both metals occupy the same position in the series.

mcqs.answer: Potassium is placed above gold in the series.
mcqs.explanation: A metal that reacts with water is higher than hydrogen and therefore higher than metals that do not react, such as gold. Hence potassium, which reacts, must be above gold in the reactivity series. Options A and B invert the order, and D is impossible because the series is a strict ranking.
